rules: Bind objectives to actual instruction and response tasks, not only scene tags. Export the coverage evidence.
Worked examples show a method; guided tasks use new values and require a learner response.
Use exact rational keys for fraction arithmetic. Equivalent unreduced fractions are accepted. Finite decimals must be exactly equal unless rounding is explicitly requested.
Misconception feedback identifies the operation or inference causing the error and explains a repair.
Teach and practise two-digit by two-digit multiplication with all four place-value partial products.
Validate diagram axes, phases, plateaus, coexistence assumptions and relative energy intervals independently of text facts.
A consequence can support a consequence claim. A direct-evidence question must ask explicitly for a stated action; no compulsory disputable inference.
A geographic objective requires licensed coordinate-derived geometry; a county register proves recall only. No route claims without roads.
Automated checks provide evidence, never academic approval, rights clearance or release authority.

objectives.statement: Represent fractions, including fractions equal to or greater than 1, on area models and a number line, naming the whole each fraction refers to.
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators, and with related denominators (e.g. halves, quarters, eighths), by using equivalent fractions.
Compare and order fractions using benchmarks (0, 1/2, 1), common denominators and the number line, and justify each comparison.

freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.question: Sketch 1 and 3/2 on equal bars and on a number line. Name the whole and explain why 3/2 exceeds 1.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.acceptableReasoning: One bar is one kilogram and each interval of length one is one kilogram. Mark 1 at 4/4, and 3/2 at six quarters, or one and a half equal bars. Two extra quarters beyond one explain why 3/2 > 1.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.feedback: Use the example reasoning to locate the unsupported step; accept different wording with valid evidence. This is formative feedback, not an official mark.

freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.question: Draw 6/4 on equal area bars, mark it on a number line and name the whole. Explain why it is beyond one.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.acceptableReasoning: Shade a full four-quarter bar and two quarters of an equal bar. Mark six quarter-steps from zero at 1.5. The amount is 6/4 of the named whole, so it exceeds 1.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.feedback: Use the example reasoning to locate the unsupported step; accept different wording with valid evidence. This is formative feedback, not an official mark.

freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.question: Order 3/4, 1/2 and 5/8. Use benchmarks and a number line to justify.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.acceptableReasoning: 1/2 < 5/8 < 3/4 because they are 4/8, 5/8 and 6/8. All lie between the one-half and one benchmarks. A number line shows this order left to right.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.feedback: Use the example reasoning to locate the unsupported step; accept different wording with valid evidence. This is formative feedback, not an official mark.

freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.question: Find 3/4 + 1/8 exactly. Also draw 6/4 on equal area bars and explain what one whole means.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.acceptableReasoning: 3/4 + 1/8 = 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8. Accept 14/16 and exact decimal 0.875. For 6/4 show one full bar and two quarter-pieces of an equal bar. The whole must be fixed and named.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.feedback: Use the example reasoning to locate the unsupported step; accept different wording with valid evidence. This is formative feedback, not an official mark.

freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.question: Give the exact remaining mass and the approximation to two decimal places. Explain why the remainder is positive and smaller than 3/4 kg.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.acceptableReasoning: 3/4 - 1/3 = 9/12 - 4/12 = 5/12 kg. Accept any exactly equivalent fraction. The explicit two-place estimate is approximately 0.42 kg. It is positive because 9 > 4 and below 3/4 because a positive amount was removed. Do not equate 0.42 with 5/12.
freeResponseAndWritingGuidance.feedback: Use the example reasoning to locate the unsupported step; accept different wording with valid evidence. This is formative feedback, not an official mark.

answerRepresentation.accepted: Equivalent a/b fractions including unreduced; exact finite decimals. No automatic simplification requirement.
answerRepresentation.rounding: Only explicitly requested two-place estimate: nearest hundredth; halfway rounded away from zero. Use approximate equality. No epsilon acceptance for exact fractions.
